name: Tyson Fresh Meats Waterloo Pork Plant - Waterloo IA

fieldNotes.truckGate: Confirmed in Street View (pano YQMIK99AN6cbsOUlyXHwhQ, captured 2026-04, heading ~272 deg). The truck drive leaves the north-south county road at 42.51042,-92.25883 and runs ~90 m west to a checkpoint: a booth/kiosk with a canopy sits in the lane, chain-link fence lines the south side of the drive, and jersey barriers channel the approach. Controlled entry, not an open driveway.
fieldNotes.guardShack: A concrete-block gatehouse with a railed roof deck, windsock, HVAC unit and a bank of red/green regulatory sign boards sits on the north side of the drive at ~42.51052,-92.25979 (footprint ~8 m x 11 m in z20/z21 satellite). A person and a parked car are visible at the adjacent lane-side booth in the 2026-04 pano. Staffed booth, so remoteGs is false.
fieldNotes.preGateStaging: About 90 m of wide paved apron between the public road and the checkpoint, entirely on Tyson pavement. Holds roughly 4-5 tractor-trailers nose to tail and is wide enough to stack two abreast.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: Set false: the ~90 m pre-gate apron plus the wide entrance flare absorb a queue, and the county road it meets is a low-volume rural two-lane. Overflow beyond ~5 trucks would still reach the road, so this is a judgement call rather than a hard negative.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: The drive measures ~11 m of pavement at the checkpoint (z20), consistent with one inbound and one outbound lane, but individual lane striping is not resolvable in either satellite or the 2026 pano. Reported 1/1 with low confidence.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Large unused paved width on both sides of the checkpoint and a very wide entrance flare at the road. Physical room for a bypass/express lane exists without new pavement.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Estimate, not a count. The main plant presents a continuous north-facing dock wall roughly 250 m long with trailers backed in at a regular rhythm (z19 imagery shows ~16 occupied/empty bay positions across a 92 m sample, about 5-6 m spacing), plus additional dock faces on the west buildings and the large white distribution building on the south-west. 60 is the midpoint estimate; the band 50+ is solid.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Very large. Herringbone trailer rows fill the north-west yard along the rail, a second fan-shaped drop yard sits west of the employee lot, and a third row runs north of the plant. Well over 50 parked trailers without tractors.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: Counted approximately 111 trailers in the south-west z18 frame alone; total across all captured imagery is roughly 230-270. Reported 250.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: Derived from ~16 acres of traced drop-yard pavement at roughly 25-30 trailers per acre including drive aisles. Approximate.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: The finished-product dock bank runs along the plant's north face while live/raw receiving and the rendering and utility buildings sit on the west and south-west of the complex, served by separate drives. Physically distinct dock clusters, but the two functions could not be labelled definitively from overhead imagery.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale deck could be positively identified. A small rectangular pad sits beside the gatehouse at z21, but it is more consistent with the building footprint than a weigh platform. Reported false rather than guessed true; a plant of this size very likely has one.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus: main process plant, a large separate white distribution/cold building to the south-west, several long narrow support buildings on the west, and outbuildings. All inside one fence.
fieldNotes.railServed: Confirmed. Rail cars are parked on a spur running east-west through the property just south of the plant (visible at 42.5083,-92.2646, z18), and the mainline runs along the north-west property edge with a second spur arcing around the east side.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: South-east edge of Waterloo IA, surrounded by row-crop fields on three sides. Per the rubric's edge-of-town/farmland test this is Rural, not Urban.
fieldNotes.perimeter: Bounded by the rail corridor on the north-west, the north-south county road on the east, the east-west county road on the south, and open field on the west. The John Deere equipment lot immediately north (rows of green tractors at 42.5119,-92.2625) was checked and EXCLUDED - it is a separate dealer property, not Tyson. Wastewater lagoons south of the south road are also excluded from the yard geofence.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: 84.4 acres computed from the perimeter ring. Covers the fenced operational yard only.
fieldNotes.verification: Web search was unavailable for this run, so no documentary confirmation was fetched. Identification rests on imagery plus the roster's ROOFTOP-precision geocode landing directly on the complex: a very large multi-building protein-processing plant with hog-scale receiving buildings, ~250 refrigerated trailers, rail service and a 1,000+ stall employee lot at the address given. Tyson's Waterloo pork plant is a long-established, publicly known site. Confidence in the operator is high but not documentarily verified in this session.
